title: Wallāh il-ʿaẓīm, it wasn't me!
goal: At the office, Maryam asks who took the cake for today's party; deny it firmly, then help her work out where it went
grammar: strong denial: aḥlif lich, mub ana, ḥatta ma + verb, ma … ay ḥad
tip: Stack your negatives for a firm denial: an oath (aḥlif lich, or wallāh il-ʿaẓīm), the denial (ma lamast-ha), then 'not even' with ḥatta ma + verb (ḥatta ma dakhalt il-maṭbakh). Inside a negative, 'anyone' is ay ḥad: ma shift ay ḥad. Put the stress on 'me' with mub ana.
dialogue: A
وين الكيكة اللي كانت في الثلاجة؟ هذي حق حفلة الوداع اليوم!
wēn il-kēka illi kānat fi th-thallāja? hādhi ḥagg ḥaflat il-wadāʿ il-yōm!
Where's the cake that was in the fridge? It's for today's farewell party!
B
مب أنا! أحلف لج، ما لمستها
mub ana! aḥlif lich, ma lamast-ha
It wasn't me! I swear to you I didn't touch it.
A
بس انت آخر واحد كان في المطبخ الصبح
bas inta ākhir wāḥid kān fi l-maṭbakh iṣ-ṣubḥ
But you were the last one in the kitchen this morning.
B
أنا حتى ما دخلت المطبخ اليوم. أنا صايم!
ana ḥatta ma dakhalt il-maṭbakh il-yōm. ana ṣāyim!
I didn't even go into the kitchen today. I'm fasting!
A
صج؟ عيل منو خذها؟ ما شفت أي حد يفتح الثلاجة؟
ṣij? ʿayal minu khadhha? ma shift ay ḥad yiftaḥ ith-thallāja?
Really? Then who took it? Didn't you see anyone open the fridge?
B
لا والله، ما شفت أي حد. وأنا مالي دخل في السالفة
la wallāh, ma shift ay ḥad. w ana māli dakhal fi s-sālfa
No, honestly, I didn't see anyone. And it's nothing to do with me.
A
زين، انت بريء لين يطلع الدليل! والمثل يقول: لا تبوق ولا تخاف
zēn, inta barīʼ lēn yiṭlaʿ id-dalīl! w il-mathal ygūl: la tbūg wala tkhāf
OK, you're innocent until the evidence turns up! As the saying goes: if you don't steal, you've nothing to fear.
B
يمكن حد حطها في ثلاجة غرفة الاجتماعات؟
yimkin ḥad ḥaṭṭha fi thallājat ghurfat il-ijtimāʿāt?
Maybe someone put it in the meeting-room fridge?
A
شوف! هني هي، الحمد لله. السموحة إني شكيت فيك
shūf! hni hiya, il-ḥamdu lillāh. is-samūḥa inni shakkēt fīk
Look! Here it is, thank God. Sorry I suspected you.
B
ما عليه. بس قلت لج: مالي دخل!
ma ʿalēh. bas gilt-lich: māli dakhal!
No problem. But I told you: nothing to do with me!
items: I swear to you (to a woman)
to a man: aḥlif lak (أحلف لك)
a masculine thing: ma lamastah (ما لمسته)
not even (before a past verb: didn't even)
it's nothing to do with me, I've no part in it
if you don't steal, you've nothing to fear (a saying)

title: Neither fixed nor phoned
goal: At a karak stand, tell Sēf the garage has had your car a week and done nothing, and decide what to do next
tip: 'Neither … nor' is la … wala: la hādha wala hādha 'neither one'. It also joins two verbs, la ḥad yrudd wala ḥad ygūl shay 'nobody answers or tells me anything', and two nouns in set phrases: la ḥiss wala khabar 'not a word from them'.
dialogue: A
شو صار على سيارتك؟ صلحوها؟
shu ṣār ʿala sayyārtak? ṣallaḥūha?
What's happening with your car? Have they fixed it?
B
لا صلحوها ولا اتصلوا! صار لي أسبوع
la ṣallaḥūha wala ittaṣlaw! ṣār-li usbūʿ
They haven't fixed it or even called! It's been a week.
A
عيل دق عليهم انت
ʿayal digg ʿalēhum inta
Then you ring them.
B
كل يوم أدق. لا حد يرد، ولا حد يقول شي
kill yōm adigg. la ḥad yrudd, wala ḥad ygūl shay
I ring every day. Nobody answers, and nobody tells me anything.
A
لا حس ولا خبر يعني؟ يمكن القطعة للحين ما وصلت من الوكالة
la ḥiss wala khabar yaʿni? yimkin il-giṭʿa lil-ḥīn ma wiṣlat min il-wakāla
Not a word, then? Maybe the part still hasn't come from the dealer.
B
يمكن. بس أنا ما عندي لا وقت ولا صبر
yimkin. bas ana ma ʿindi la wagt wala ṣabir
Maybe. But I've got neither the time nor the patience.
A
وانت من غير سيارة، لا رحت ولا ييت هالأسبوع
w inta min ghēr sayyāra, la riḥt wala yīt hal-usbūʿ
And without a car, you haven't been anywhere this week.
B
بالضبط. حتى الجامعة أروح لها بالتاكسي
biẓ-ẓabṭ. ḥatta l-jāmʿa arūḥ-lha bit-tāksi
Exactly. Even uni, I go by taxi.
A
زين، شو بتسوي؟ بتعطيهم وقت ولّا بتاخذها مكان ثاني؟
zēn, shu bitsawwi? bitʿaṭīhum wagt walla bitākhidhha makān thāni?
So what will you do? Give them time, or take it somewhere else?
B
لا هذا ولا هذا. بروح لهم باكر الصبح بنفسي
la hādha wala hādha. barūḥ-lhum bāchir iṣ-ṣubḥ b-nafsi
Neither. I'll go and see them tomorrow morning myself.
items: neither (one), neither one nor the other
not a word, no news at all (lit. no sound and no news)
ما عندي لا وقت ولا صبر
ma ʿindi la wagt wala ṣabir
I've got neither the time nor the patience
the spare parts: giṭaʿ il-ghiyār (قطع الغيار); (recognise)
you haven't been anywhere (lit. you neither went nor came) (to a man)
to a woman: la riḥti wala yīti; (recognise)
I go there by taxi (a feminine place)
a masculine thing: lil-ḥīn ma wiṣal (للحين ما وصل)

title: We only see you at Eid!
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, take his teasing about how rarely you visit, and talk about Rāshid, who thinks of nothing but football
grammar: 'only' as ma … illa (nothing but, no one but)
tip: Gulf says 'only' as 'not … except': ma … illa. ma baga illa l-imtiḥānāt 'only the exams are left'; ma yfakkir illa fi l-kūra 'he thinks of nothing but football'. Elders use it to tease: ma nshūfak illa fi l-aʿyād 'we only see you at Eid'.
dialogue: A
هلا والله بسالم! ما نشوفك إلا في الأعياد يا ولدي
hala wallāh b-Sālim! ma nshūfak illa fi l-aʿyād yā wildi
Well, hello, Sālim! We only ever see you at Eid, son.
B
السموحة يا عمي، الشغل والدراسة ما خلوا لي وقت
is-samūḥa yā ʿammi, ish-shughul w id-dirāsa ma khallaw-li wagt
Forgive me, uncle; work and studies haven't left me any time.
A
مسموح يا ولدي. وشحال الدراسة؟
masmūḥ yā wildi. w shḥāl id-dirāsa?
No need, son. And how are your studies?
B
الحمد لله، ما بقى إلا الامتحانات. وراشد شحاله؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh, ma baga illa l-imtiḥānāt. w Rāshid shḥālah?
Fine, thank God; only the exams are left. And how's Rāshid?
A
راشد؟ ما يفكر إلا في الكورة، وراسه يابس، ما يسمع كلامي
Rāshid? ma yfakkir illa fi l-kūra, w rāsah yābis, ma yismaʿ kalāmi
Rāshid? He thinks of nothing but football, and he's pig-headed; he won't listen to me.
B
بس امتحاناته قريبة. ما يذاكر أبد؟
bas imtiḥānātah garība. ma ydhākir abad?
But his exams are soon. Doesn't he study at all?
A
ولا ساعة. هالولد ما يسمع إلا من ولد عمه، سيف
wala sāʿa. hal-walad ma yismaʿ illa min wild ʿammah, Sēf
Not for an hour. That boy listens to no one but his cousin, Sēf.
B
بس سيف عنيد بعد يا عمي!
bas Sēf ʿanīd baʿad yā ʿammi!
But Sēf's stubborn too, uncle!
A
صح كلامك. بس يقولون: ما يفل الحديد إلا الحديد
ṣaḥḥ kalāmak. bas ygūlūn: ma yfill il-ḥadīd illa l-ḥadīd
You're right. But as they say, only iron can bend iron.
B
يعني ما يقدر على راشد إلا سيف!
yaʿni ma yigdar ʿala Rāshid illa Sēf!
So only Sēf can handle Rāshid!
items: we only ever see you (at, on…) (to a man)
to a woman: ma nshūfich illa (ما نشوفج إلا)
he listens to no one but
he doesn't study, he doesn't revise
he's pig-headed (lit. his head is dry)
only iron can bend iron (it takes a tough one to handle a tough one) (a saying)

title: Never seen a camel race
goal: At university, Sēf invites you to the camel races with Bū Rāshid; admit you've never been, and agree to an early start
grammar: negative concord: ma … ay, wala marra, maḥḥad + verb
tip: In a negative sentence every 'any' word stays negative: ma ʿindi ay fikra 'I haven't any idea', maḥḥad biyisʼalak 'no one will ask you', wala marra 'not once'. And ma yiḥtāj + verb says 'there's no need to': ma yiḥtāj taʿarf shay.
dialogue: A
بو راشد بيروح سباق الهجن يوم الجمعة. تبي تيي؟
Bū Rāshid biyrūḥ sibāg il-hijin yōm il-jumʿa. tabi tiyi?
Bū Rāshid's going to the camel races on Friday. Do you want to come?
B
أكيد! عمري ما شفت ولا سباق
akīd! ʿumri ma shift wala sibāg
Definitely! I've never seen a single race in my life.
A
صج؟ ولا مرة؟ ولا حتى في التلفزيون؟
ṣij? wala marra? wala ḥatta fi t-tilfizyōn?
Really? Not once? Not even on TV?
B
ولا مرة. وما أعرف أي شي عنها
wala marra. w ma aʿarf ay shay ʿanha
Not once. And I don't know anything about them.
A
ما يحتاج تعرف شي. تعال وشوف بس
ma yiḥtāj taʿarf shay. taʿāl w shūf bas
You don't need to know anything. Just come and watch.
B
بس ما أعرف أي حد هناك غيركم
bas ma aʿarf ay ḥad hnāk ghērkum
But I don't know anyone there apart from you.
A
لا تخاف، محد بيسألك شي. وبو راشد يعرف كل الناس هناك
la tkhāf, maḥḥad biyisʼalak shay. w Bū Rāshid yaʿarf kill in-nās hnāk
Don't worry, nobody's going to ask you anything. And Bū Rāshid knows everyone there.
B
زين، ما عندي مانع. متى نتحرك؟
zēn, ma ʿindi māniʿ. mita nitḥarrak?
OK, I don't mind. When do we set off?
A
قبل الفجر. والسباق الصبح بدري، يعني ما في نوم!
gabil il-fajr. w is-sibāg iṣ-ṣubḥ badri, yaʿni ma fī nōm!
Before dawn. The race is early in the morning, so no lie-in!
B
ما في مشكلة. بكون جاهز من الساعة أربع
ma fī mushkila. bakūn jāhiz min is-sāʿa arbaʿ
No problem. I'll be ready from four o'clock.
items: there's no need (to), you don't need (to)
I don't mind, I've no objection
we set off, we get going
no sleep, no lie-in (lit. there's no sleep)
culture: Camel racing is a winter sport in the UAE, with races held early in the morning at tracks such as Al Marmoom near Dubai. Since the 2000s the camels have been ridden by small remote-controlled robot jockeys instead of children, and owners drive alongside the track in their cars, following the race.

title: Dream on, Rāshid!
goal: Outside the majlis, Rāshid (17) begs to drive your car 'just once round the block'; refuse firmly, with humour, and don't give in
grammar: strong refusal: la tiḥlam, w lō + verb … ma, insa l-mawẓūʿ
tip: Refuse with a stack: la tiḥlam 'dream on', then 'even if' with w lō: w lō tʿaṭīni malyōn, ma baʿṭīk il-miftāḥ 'even if you gave me a million, I wouldn't give you the key'. Close it with insa l-mawẓūʿ 'forget it'. Keep these for friends and younger people.
dialogue: A
برو، عطني مفتاح سيارتك! بس لفة وحدة حول المجلس
brō, ʿaṭni miftāḥ sayyārtak! bas laffa waḥda ḥōl il-majlis
Bro, give me your car key! Just one spin round the majlis.
B
مستحيل! انت ما عندك رخصة
mustaḥīl! inta ma ʿindak rukhṣa
No way! You haven't got a licence.
A
بس أعرف أسوق! أبوي علمني في البر
bas aʿarf asūg! ubūy ʿallamni fi l-barr
But I know how to drive! My dad taught me in the desert.
B
لا تحلم. ولو تعطيني مليون، ما بعطيك المفتاح
la tiḥlam. w lō tʿaṭīni malyōn, ma baʿṭīk il-miftāḥ
Dream on. Even if you gave me a million, I wouldn't give you the key.
A
حرام عليك! محد بيدري، والله
ḥarām ʿalēk! maḥḥad biydri, wallāh
Come on, that's mean! Nobody'll know, honestly.
B
أبوك بيدري، وبيذبحني أنا قبلك
ubūk biydri, w biydhbaḥni ana gablak
Your dad will know, and he'll kill me before he kills you.
A
أوكي، عيل بس في الباركنج؟ عشر دقايق، وبعدين خلاص
ōkē, ʿayal bas fi l-bārking? ʿashr dagāyig, w baʿdēn khalāṣ
OK, then just in the car park? Ten minutes, and then that's it.
B
انسى الموضوع يا راشد. لا في الباركنج ولا في الشارع
insa l-mawẓūʿ yā Rāshid. la fi l-bārking wala fi sh-shāriʿ
Forget it, Rāshid. Not in the car park, not on the road.
A
زين، بس يوم أطلع الرخصة، أول سيارة بسوقها سيارتك!
zēn, bas yōm aṭallaʿ ir-rukhṣa, awwal sayyāra basūgha sayyārtak!
Fine, but when I get my licence, the first car I drive will be yours!
B
يصير خير! بس مب قبل
yṣīr khēr! bas mub gabil
We'll see! But not before.
items: dream on, forget it (lit. don't dream) (to a man) (friends only)
to a woman: la tiḥlamīn (لا تحلمين)
even if you gave me (to a man)
to a woman: the same (ولو تعطيني)
I won't give you (to a man)
to a woman: ma baʿṭīch (ما بعطيج)
forget it, drop it (to a man)
to a woman: insay il-mawẓūʿ (انسي الموضوع)
he'll kill me (joking: he'll be furious with me)
I know how to drive, I can drive
we'll see, maybe later (lit. good will happen)
one spin, one quick drive round
culture: In the UAE you must be at least 18 to get a licence to drive a car, and driving without one is a traffic offence. Teenagers in the Gulf often learn to drive with a parent out in the desert, but on the roads it's the licence that counts.
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search a tutoring site for «Emirati Arabic tutor»), talk for 10 minutes. First tell them about three things you've never done (ʿumri ma…, wala marra). Then ask them to accuse you, as a joke, of something; deny it firmly (wallāh il-ʿaẓīm, mub ana, māli dakhal) and refuse what they ask (la tiḥlam, w lō…).

title: Whoever wins, I'm with them!
goal: At university, Sēf is organising a five-a-side game for Thursday night; sort out who plays, who pays and whose team you're on
grammar: free relatives: illi 'whoever, whatever', shu ma / wēn ma 'whatever, wherever'
tip: illi with no noun before it means 'whoever' or 'whatever': illi yfūz 'whoever wins', illi ʿindah 'whatever he's got'. shu ma, wēn ma and minu ma make 'whatever, wherever, whoever': shu ma ṣār 'whatever happens', wēn ma ḥaṭṭētak 'wherever I put you'.
dialogue: A
الخميس بنلعب كورة في الملعب اللي يم الجامعة. تبي تلعب؟
il-khamīs binilʿab kūra fi l-malʿab illi yamm il-jāmʿa. tabi tilʿab?
On Thursday we're playing football at the pitch next to the university. Do you want to play?
B
أكيد! منو بيلعب ويانا؟
akīd! minu biyilʿab wiyyāna?
Sure! Who's playing with us?
A
اللي يبي ييي، ييي. بس اللي يتأخر يدفع حق الملعب!
illi yabi yiyi, yiyi. bas illi yitʼakhkhar yidfaʿ ḥagg il-malʿab!
Whoever wants to come can come. But whoever's late pays for the pitch!
B
شو ما صار، أنا بكون هناك قبل الساعة ثمان
shu ma ṣār, ana bakūn hnāk gabil is-sāʿa thamān
Whatever happens, I'll be there before eight.
A
وكل واحد يلبس اللي عنده، ما يحتاج تشتري شي
w kill wāḥid yilbis illi ʿindah, ma yiḥtāj tishtiri shay
And everyone wears whatever they've got; no need to buy anything.
B
زين. وأنا في أي فريق؟
zēn. w ana fi ay farīg?
OK. And which team am I on?
A
مع منو ما تبي. اختار انت
maʿa minu ma tabi. ikhtār inta
With whoever you like. You choose.
B
بلعب مع اللي يفوز!
balʿab maʿa illi yfūz!
I'll play with whoever wins!
A
لا لا، ما يصير جي! وين ما حطيتك تلعب، واللي يزعل يروح البيت
la la, ma yṣīr chidhi! wēn ma ḥaṭṭētak tilʿab, w illi yizʿal yrūḥ il-bēt
No, no, you can't do that! You play wherever I put you, and whoever sulks goes home.
B
خلاص، اللي تشوفه يا كابتن
khalāṣ, illi tshūfah yā kābtin
Fine, whatever you say, captain.
items: with whoever you like (to a man)
to a woman: maʿa minu ma tabīn (مع منو ما تبين)
captain! (to the one in charge, joking) (friends only)

title: Weren't you the one who said 'leave it to me'?
goal: On Thursday evening, Sēf admits he forgot to book the pitch; tell him off, as a friend, and let him put it right
grammar: non-restrictive illi huwa; reproaching: mub inta illi …?, ʿēb ʿalēk
tip: Reproach a friend with a question: mub inta illi gilt 'khallha ʿalay'? 'weren't you the one who said leave it to me?' Add a fact about someone with illi huwa: wild ʿammi, illi huwa yishtaghil fi nādi 'my cousin, who works at a club'. ʿēb ʿalēk is for friends only.
dialogue: A
يا ريال، الملعب محجوز! ما في مكان الليلة
yā rayyāl, il-malʿab maḥjūz! ma fī makān il-lēla
Mate, the pitch is booked! There's no slot tonight.
B
شلون محجوز؟ مب انت اللي قلت خلها علي؟
shlōn maḥjūz? mub inta illi gilt khallha ʿalay?
What do you mean, booked? Weren't you the one who said 'leave it to me'?
A
هيه... بس نسيت أحجز. السموحة
hē… bas nisēt aḥjiz. is-samūḥa
Yes… but I forgot to book. Sorry.
B
عيب عليك! والشباب، اللي بعضهم ياي من الشارقة، الحين في الطريق
ʿēb ʿalēk! w ish-shabāb, illi baʿaẓhum yāy min ish-Shārja, il-ḥīn fi ṭ-ṭarīg
You should be ashamed! And the guys, some of whom are coming from Sharjah, are on their way now.
A
أدري، الغلط مني. شو أقول؟ الشرهة علي
adri, il-ghalaṭ minni. shu agūl? ish-sharha ʿalay
I know, it's my fault. What can I say? The blame's on me.
B
ما توقعتها منك يا سيف. شو هالحركة؟
ma twaggaʿt-ha minnak yā Sēf. shu hal-ḥaraka?
I didn't expect that from you, Sēf. What kind of move is that?
A
خلاص، بدق على ولد عمي، اللي هو يشتغل في نادي. يمكن عنده ملعب
khalāṣ, badigg ʿala wild ʿammi, illi huwa yishtaghil fi nādi. yimkin ʿindah malʿab
OK, I'll ring my cousin, who works at a club. Maybe he's got a pitch.
B
زين، بس هالمرة لا تنسى!
zēn, bas hal-marra la tinsa!
OK, but this time don't forget!
A
أبشر. والعشا الليلة علي، والله
abshir. w il-ʿasha l-lēla ʿalay, wallāh
Consider it done. And tonight's dinner is on me, I promise.
B
ما عليه، المهم نلعب
ma ʿalēh, il-muhimm nilʿab
Never mind; what matters is that we play.
items: weren't you the one who…? (to a man)
to a woman: mub inti illi (مب انتي اللي)
you should be ashamed, shame on you (to a man) (friends only)
to a woman: ʿēb ʿalēch (عيب عليج)
I didn't expect that from you (to a man)
to a woman: ma twaggaʿt-ha minnich (ما توقعتها منج)
what kind of move is that? what's that about? (friends only)
who (by the way) is, who (adding a fact about someone)
the blame's on me, it's my fault (I should have known)

title: I wonder what they'll ask
goal: At the office, Maryam tells you that you're presenting to the client tomorrow; say how nervous you are, and get her help to prepare
grammar: embedded questions: ma aʿarf shu / min wēn …, yā tara shu …
tip: Put a question inside a sentence with no change of word order: ma aʿarf shu agūl 'I don't know what to say'; ma aʿarf min wēn abda 'I don't know where to start'. yā tara + question is 'I wonder…': yā tara shu biyisʼalūn? 'I wonder what they'll ask?'
dialogue: A
المدير يبيك تقدم العرض حق العميل باكر
il-mudīr yabīk tgaddim il-ʿarẓ ḥagg il-ʿamīl bāchir
The manager wants you to give the presentation to the client tomorrow.
B
أنا؟ ما تدرين شكثر أنا متوتر من هالشي
ana? ma tadrīn shkuthur ana mitwattir min hash-shay
Me? You've no idea how nervous I get about that sort of thing.
A
ليش؟ انت تعرف المشروع أحسن من أي حد
lēsh? inta taʿarf il-mashrūʿ aḥsan min ay ḥad
Why? You know the project better than anyone.
B
يا ترا شو بيسألون؟ ما أعرف من وين أبدا
yā tara shu biyisʼalūn? ma aʿarf min wēn abda
I wonder what they'll ask? I don't know where to start.
A
خلنا نكتب الأسئلة اللي متوقعينها، ونتدرب عليها الحين
khallna niktib il-asʼila illi mitwaggʿīnha, w nitdarrab ʿalēha l-ḥīn
Let's write down the questions we expect, and practise them now.
B
زين. بس ما أعرف شو أقول لهم عن الأرقام
zēn. bas ma aʿarf shu agūl-lhum ʿan il-argām
OK. But I don't know what to tell them about the figures.
A
قول لهم الصج، وإذا ما تعرف شي، قول: بنرد عليكم
gūl-lhum iṣ-ṣij, w idha ma taʿarf shay, gūl: binrudd ʿalēkum
Tell them the truth, and if you don't know something, say: we'll get back to you.
B
فكرة حلوة. تعرفين منو بيحضر من عندهم؟
fikra ḥilwa. taʿarfīn minu biyiḥẓar min ʿind-hum?
Good idea. Do you know who's coming from their side?
A
ما أدري بالضبط، بس أظن المديرة حقهم بنفسها
ma adri biẓ-ẓabṭ, bas aẓunn il-mudīra ḥagg-hum b-nafsha
I don't know exactly, but I think their manager herself.
B
الله يستر! خلينا نبدا الحين
allāh yistur! khallna nibda l-ḥīn
Heaven help me! Let's start now.
items: I don't know where to start
I don't know what to say
you give the presentation, you present (to a man)
to a woman: tgaddmīn il-ʿarẓ (تقدمين العرض)
we'll get back to you (to a group)
to one man: binrudd ʿalēk; to one woman: binrudd ʿalēch
who's coming? who'll be there? (to a meeting)

title: Who says you need a degree?
goal: In the majlis, with Sēf there, Rāshid says he'll skip university and become a YouTuber; argue with him using questions, and find a middle way
grammar: rhetorical questions in an argument: minu gāl inn…?, shu l-fāyda min…?, wēn il-mushkila?
tip: Argue with questions that don't want an answer: minu gāl inn…? 'who says…?', shu l-fāyda min…? 'what's the point of…?', wēn il-mushkila? 'where's the problem?'. A question can also push back gently: lēsh titʿib nafsak? 'why wear yourself out?'
dialogue: A
ليش أدرس أربع سنين؟ أبي أصير يوتيوبر وبس
lēsh adris arbaʿ sinīn? abi aṣīr yūtyūbar w bas
Why study for four years? I just want to be a YouTuber.
B
ومنو قال إن اليوتيوبر ما يحتاج شهادة؟
w minu gāl inn il-yūtyūbar ma yiḥtāj shahāda?
And who says a YouTuber doesn't need a degree?
A
شو الفايدة من الشهادة؟ في ناس عندهم ملايين المتابعين بدون جامعة
shu l-fāyda min ish-shahāda? fī nās ʿind-hum malāyīn il-mutābiʿīn bidūn jāmʿa
What's the point of a degree? There are people with millions of followers and no university.
B
وكم واحد منهم؟ واحد من كل ألف؟
w cham wāḥid minhum? wāḥid min kill alf?
And how many of them are there? One in every thousand?
A
وين المشكلة؟ أجرب، وإذا ما نفع، أدرس بعدين
wēn il-mushkila? ajarrib, w idha ma nifaʿ, adris baʿdēn
Where's the problem? I'll try, and if it doesn't work, I'll study later.
B
وبعد كم سنة؟ تبدا الجامعة وكل ربعك متخرجين؟
w baʿd cham sana? tibda l-jāmʿa w kill rabʿak mitkharrjīn?
And after how many years? Start university when all your mates have graduated?
A
ليش لا؟ في ناس يبدون متأخر
lēsh la? fī nās yibdūn mitʼakhkhir
Why not? Some people start late.
B
صح، بس ليش تتعب نفسك؟ تقدر تسوي الثنتين
ṣaḥḥ, bas lēsh titʿib nafsak? tigdar tsawwi th-thintēn
True, but why wear yourself out? You can do both.
A
يعني أدرس وأصور مع بعض؟ والله فكرة
yaʿni adris w aṣawwir maʿa baʿaẓ? wallāh fikra
You mean study and film at the same time? That's an idea.
B
أكيد! وأول فيديو: يوم في حياة طالب جامعة!
akīd! w awwal fīdyō: yōm fi ḥayāt ṭālib jāmʿa!
Of course! And your first video: a day in the life of a uni student!
items: where's the problem? what's wrong with that?
and how many of them are there (really)?
why wear yourself out? why make it hard for yourself? (to a man)
to a woman: lēsh titʿbīn nafsich? (ليش تتعبين نفسج؟)
a man: mitkharrij (متخرج); a woman: mitkharrja (متخرجة)
culture: In the UAE, people who advertise products or services on social media need a permit from the UAE Media Council, and the rules were tightened in 2025. So being a 'YouTuber' as a job can involve paperwork as well as filming.

title: Shu hal-jamāl! Kayaking in Hatta
goal: On a winter trip to Hatta with Sēf, marvel at the lake and the mountains, and admit you should have come before
grammar: exclamatives: shu hal-…!, shay khayāl!, wala arwaʿ; recycle: shkuthur, yā salām
tip: Marvel with shu hal- + noun: shu hal-jamāl! 'how beautiful!'. Short exclamations: shay khayāl! 'out of this world!', wala arwaʿ 'nothing beats it'. ma twaggaʿt inn… 'I didn't expect…' marvels too: ma twaggaʿt inn Ḥatta b-hal-ḥalāwa.
dialogue: A
شوف الماي! شو هالجمال!
shūf il-māy! shu hal-jamāl!
Look at the water! How beautiful!
B
سبحان الله! ما توقعت إن حتا بهالحلاوة
subḥān allāh! ma twaggaʿt inn Ḥatta b-hal-ḥalāwa
Amazing! I didn't expect Hatta to be this lovely.
A
وشكثر الماي صافي! تقدر تشوف الصخر تحت
w shkuthur il-māy ṣāfi! tigdar tshūf iṣ-ṣakhar taḥt
And the water's so clear! You can see the rocks underneath.
B
يا سلام! والجبال حوالينا، شي خيال!
yā salām! w il-jibāl ḥawālēna, shay khayāl!
Wow! And the mountains all around us, it's out of this world!
A
قلت لك! ولا أروع من حتا في الشتا
gilt-lak! wala arwaʿ min Ḥatta fi sh-shita
I told you! Nothing beats Hatta in winter.
B
والهوا بارد وحلو. مب مثل زحمة دبي
w il-hawa bārid w ḥilu. mub mithil zaḥmat Dbayy
And the air's cool and lovely. Not like the crowds in Dubai.
A
يلا، خلنا ناخذ الكاياك لين آخر السد
yalla, khallna nākhidh il-kāyāk lēn ākhir is-sadd
Come on, let's take the kayak to the far end of the dam.
B
ليش ما ييت هني من قبل؟ ضيعت وايد!
lēsh ma yīt hni min gabil? ẓayyaʿt wāyid!
Why didn't I come here before? I've missed out on so much!
A
لأنك كل ويكند في المول!
lann-ak kill wīkind fi l-mōl!
Because you're at the mall every weekend!
B
خلاص، من اليوم ولا مول، بس جبال!
khalāṣ, min il-yōm wala mōl, bas jibāl!
Right, from today, no more malls, just mountains!
items: how beautiful! (lit. what is this beauty)
it's out of this world! it's amazing!
nothing beats it, it couldn't be better
culture: Hatta is a mountain town in the Hajar Mountains, part of the emirate of Dubai, about an hour and a half's drive from the city. In the cooler months people go there for the hiking trails and to kayak on the lake behind Hatta Dam.
task: This week: search YouTube for «رحلة حتا» or «يومياتي في حتا» (a Hatta trip vlog) and watch 10 minutes. Within a minute you should hear شو / مب; if you hear سوف or ليس all the time, pick another clip. Note every exclamation (shu hal-…, subḥān allāh, yā salām). Then record a 2-minute voice note to Sēf describing a place that amazed you.

title: Even though I was nervous
goal: At the office, Maryam tells you the client has approved the project; admit what went wrong in your presentation, and hear why it worked anyway
grammar: concessives: maʿa inni, walaw innah, w maʿa hādha, ṣaḥḥ innah … bas
tip: Concede, then turn: maʿa inni kint mitwattir 'even though I was nervous'; walaw innhum shāfōha 'even though they saw them'. Turn with w maʿa hādha 'and yet' or bas. ṣaḥḥ innah … bas … 'it's true that…, but…' admits a point before you answer it.
dialogue: A
مبروك! العميل وافق على المشروع
mabrūk! il-ʿamīl wāfag ʿala l-mashrūʿ
Congratulations! The client has approved the project.
B
الله يبارك فيج! مع إني كنت متوتر وايد
allāh ybārik fīch! maʿa inni kint mitwattir wāyid
Thank you! Even though I was really nervous.
A
ومع هذا، العرض كان واضح ومرتب
w maʿa hādha, il-ʿarẓ kān wāẓiḥ w mrattab
And yet the presentation was clear and well organised.
B
صح إنه في كم غلطة، بس الحمد لله ما انتبهوا
ṣaḥḥ innah fī cham ghalṭa, bas il-ḥamdu lillāh ma intabhaw
It's true there were a few mistakes, but thank God they didn't notice.
A
لا، انتبهوا! بس ولو إنهم شافوها، المشروع عجبهم
la, intabhaw! bas walaw innhum shāfōha, il-mashrūʿ ʿijabhum
Oh, they noticed! But even though they saw them, they liked the project.
B
يعني رغم الأغلاط وافقوا؟
yaʿni raghm il-aghlāṭ wāfgaw?
So they approved it despite the mistakes?
A
هيه. حتى لو الأرقام ما كانت كاملة، الفكرة كانت قوية
hē. ḥatta lō l-argām ma kānat kāmla, il-fikra kānat gawiyya
Yes. Even if the figures weren't complete, the idea was strong.
B
على كل حال، المرة الياية بكون أحسن
ʿala kill ḥāl, il-marra l-yāya bakūn aḥsan
Anyway, next time I'll be better.
A
أكيد. وبالرغم من كل شي، الفريق كله فخور فيك
akīd. w bir-raghm min kill shay, il-farīg killah fakhūr fīk
Of course. And in spite of everything, the whole team is proud of you.
B
مشكورة يا مريم، من غير مساعدتج ما كنت قدرت
mashkūra yā Maryam, min ghēr musāʿadtich ma kint gidart
Thank you, Maryam; without your help I couldn't have done it.
items: even though he, even though it
even though they: walaw innhum (ولو إنهم)
they liked it (lit. it pleased them)
to a woman: fakhūr fīch (فخور فيج); (recognise)

title: OK, you beat me. I admit it
goal: At your flat in Mirdif, Sēf beats you at football on the PlayStation; admit he played better, but get your own point in
grammar: conceding: aʿtarif, ma agūl la, bas…; recycle: maʿa inni, ʿala kill ḥāl
tip: Concede in steps: say it (zēn, ghalabtni), admit it (aʿtarif), then add your point with bas: ma agūl la, bas… 'I won't say no, but…'. Close with ʿala kill ḥāl 'anyway'. A good loser also teases back: mub ʿudhur! 'it's not an excuse!'
dialogue: A
خمسة ثلاثة! شفت؟ قلت لك ما تقدر علي
khamsa thalātha! shift? gilt-lak ma tigdar ʿalay
Five three! See? I told you you couldn't handle me.
B
زين، غلبتني. أعترف
zēn, ghalabtni. aʿtarif
OK, you beat me. I admit it.
A
وتعترف إني أحسن منك؟
w tiʿtarif inni aḥsan minnak?
And you admit I'm better than you?
B
ما أقول لا، بس في الشوط الأول ما ركزت
ma agūl la, bas fi sh-shōṭ il-awwal ma rakkazt
I won't say no, but I wasn't focused in the first half.
A
كل مرة نفس العذر! ما ركزت، الجويستك خربان، النت بطيء
kill marra nafs il-ʿudhur! ma rakkazt, il-jōystik kharbān, in-nit baṭīʼ
The same excuse every time! I wasn't focused, the controller's broken, the internet's slow.
B
مب عذر! ومع إني خسرت، لعبت زين في الشوط الثاني
mub ʿudhur! w maʿa inni khisart, liʿabt zēn fi sh-shōṭ ith-thāni
It's not an excuse! And even though I lost, I played well in the second half.
A
صح، أعترف إن الهدف الثالث حقك كان حلو
ṣaḥḥ, aʿtarif inn il-hadaf ith-thālith ḥaggak kān ḥilu
True, I admit your third goal was a nice one.
B
على كل حال، المرة الياية بتشوف
ʿala kill ḥāl, il-marra l-yāya bitshūf
Anyway, next time you'll see.
A
إن شاء الله! بس لين ذاك اليوم، أنا البطل. جولة ثانية؟
in shāʼ allāh! bas lēn dhāk il-yōm, ana l-baṭal. jōla thānya?
God willing! But until that day, I'm the champion. Another round?
B
لا تبالغ! يلا، جولة ثانية
la tbālig! yalla, jōla thānya
Don't get carried away! Go on, another round.
items: I won't say no (to that), I can't deny it
an excuse: ʿudhur (عذر); the same excuse: nafs il-ʿudhur
I wasn't focused, I didn't concentrate
you weren't focused: ma rakkazt (to a man), ma rakkazti (to a woman)

title: I mean ten, not twenty
goal: In the team meeting, give Maryam and the team this month's sales figures, catch your own slip, and say it again more clearly
grammar: repair: agṣid, khallni agūlha b-ṭarīga thānya, zallat lisān
tip: Correct yourself at once with la, agṣid… 'no, I mean…'. For a slip, say zallat lisān. If people don't follow, start again: khallni agūlha b-ṭarīga thānya 'let me put it another way'. gaṣdi inn… 'what I mean is…' explains.
dialogue: A
يلا، عطنا أرقام المبيعات حق هالشهر
yalla, ʿaṭna argām il-mabīʿāt ḥagg hash-shahar
Go on, give us this month's sales figures.
B
زادت عشرين بالمية... لا، أقصد عشرة
zādat ʿishrīn bil-miya… la, agṣid ʿashra
They went up twenty per cent… no, I mean ten.
A
عشرة ولّا عشرين؟ في فرق!
ʿashra walla ʿishrīn? fī farg!
Ten or twenty? There's a difference!
B
السموحة، زلة لسان. عشرة بالمية، مب عشرين
is-samūḥa, zallat lisān. ʿashra bil-miya, mub ʿishrīn
Sorry, a slip of the tongue. Ten per cent, not twenty.
A
ما عليه. وليش هالشهر أحسن من اللي قبله؟
ma ʿalēh. w lēsh hash-shahar aḥsan min illi gablah?
No problem. And why is this month better than the one before?
B
عشان... خلني أقولها بطريقة ثانية: الناس اشتروا أكثر لأن الأسعار نزلت
ʿashān… khallni agūlha b-ṭarīga thānya: in-nās ishtaraw akthar lann il-asʿār nizlat
Because… let me put it another way: people bought more because prices came down.
A
يعني الخصم هو السبب؟
yaʿni l-khaṣim huwa s-sabab?
So the discount is the reason?
B
مب بس. قصدي إن الخصم ساعد، بس مب هو السبب الوحيد
mub bas. gaṣdi inn il-khaṣim sāʿad, bas mub huwa s-sabab il-waḥīd
Not only. What I mean is that the discount helped, but it isn't the only reason.
A
واضح. لازم نشوف الأرقام بدون الخصم بعد
wāẓiḥ. lāzim nshūf il-argām bidūn il-khaṣim baʿad
Clear. We need to see the figures without the discount as well.
B
بالضبط. بطرش لج التفاصيل بعد الاجتماع
biẓ-ẓabṭ. baṭarrish-lich it-tafāṣīl baʿd il-ijtimāʿ
Exactly. I'll send you the details after the meeting.
items: let me put it another way: khallni agūlha b-ṭarīga thānya
the one before (it), the previous one (m.)
a feminine noun: illi gabilha (اللي قبلها)

title: Between you and me, Fahad
goal: On a call with Fahad in Kuwait, tell him, just between you, that you're staying in Dubai after you graduate, and that your mum doesn't know yet
grammar: parentheticals: bēni w bēnak, ṣaddigni, ʿala ḥasab ʿilmi, allāh yiḥfaẓ- after naming a parent
tip: Asides go in the middle of a sentence: bas, bēni w bēnak, bagʿid… 'but, between you and me, I'm staying…'. ṣaddigni 'believe me' adds weight. After naming a parent, Gulf speakers often add a blessing: ummi, allāh yiḥfaẓha, … 'my mum, God keep her, …'.
dialogue: A
هلا والله! شلونك؟ شنو أخبار دبي؟
hala wallāh! shlōnak? shinu akhbār Dbayy?
Hey! How are you? What's the news from Dubai?
B
هلا فيك! كل شي زين. بس بيني وبينك، بقعد في دبي بعد التخرج
hala fīk! kill shay zēn. bas bēni w bēnak, bagʿid fi Dbayy baʿd it-takharruj
Hi! All good. But between you and me, I'm staying in Dubai after I graduate.
A
صج؟ يعني قبلت الوظيفة؟ وأهلك يدرون؟
ṣij? yaʿni gibalt il-waẓīfa? w ahlak yadrūn?
Really? So you've taken the job? Does your family know?
B
للحين لا. وصدقني، أمي، الله يحفظها، بتزعل
lil-ḥīn la. w ṣaddigni, ummi, allāh yiḥfaẓha, bitizʿal
Not yet. And believe me, my mum, God keep her, will be upset.
A
طبيعي، كل الأمهات جذي. بس الشغل زين، صح؟
ṭabīʿi, kill il-ummahāt chidhi. bas ish-shughul zēn, ṣaḥḥ?
That's normal; all mums are like that. But the job's good, right?
B
هيه، وعلى حسب علمي، الراتب بيزيد بعد سنة
hē, w ʿala ḥasab ʿilmi, ir-rātib biyzīd baʿd sana
Yes, and as far as I know, the salary goes up after a year.
A
خوش! مع احترامي لأمك، هذي فرصتك
khōsh! maʿa iḥtirāmi l-ummak, hādhi furṣtak
Great! With all respect to your mum, this is your chance.
B
أدري. بس والله، صعب أقول لها
adri. bas wallāh, ṣaʿb agūl-lha
I know. But honestly, it's hard to tell her.
A
الحق يقال، صعب. بس كلمها بنفسك، مب بالواتساب
il-ḥagg yingāl, ṣaʿb. bas kallimha b-nafsak, mub bil-wātsāb
Truth be told, it is hard. But talk to her yourself, not on WhatsApp.
B
فكرة زينة. إن شاء الله بكلمها هالويكند
fikra zēna. in shāʼ allāh bakallimha hal-wīkind
Good idea. I'll talk to her this weekend, God willing.
items: between you and me (to a man)
to a woman: bēni w bēnich (بيني وبينج)
truth be told, to be fair (formal)

title: Staying? Staying.
goal: At a karak stand, Sēf fires quick questions about your decision to stay in Dubai; answer him in short replies, the way friends do
grammar: ellipsis and short replies: answering with one word or phrase, leaving out what's known
tip: Between friends, leave out what you both know. Answer with the key word: bitigʿid walla bitirjaʿ? — bagʿid. Answer a 'when' with just the time: il-wīkind. A short reply isn't rude in fast talk, and shwayy, akīd 'a bit, for sure' is enough.
dialogue: A
ها؟ قررت؟ بتقعد ولّا بترجع لندن؟
hā? garrart? bitigʿid walla bitirjaʿ Landan?
So? Have you decided? Are you staying, or going back to London?
B
بقعد، إن شاء الله
bagʿid, in shāʼ allāh
Staying, God willing.
A
صج؟ وأهلك؟
ṣij? w ahlak?
Really? And your family?
B
للحين ما قلت لهم. الويكند
lil-ḥīn ma gilt-lhum. il-wīkind
I haven't told them yet. At the weekend.
A
بس جي؟ بالتلفون؟
bas chī? bit-tilifōn?
Just like that? On the phone?
B
لا، فيديو. وأخوي الكبير ويانا
la, fīdyō. w akhūy il-kbīr wiyyāna
No, video. With my eldest brother on it too.
A
وأمك؟ بتزعل؟ بتبكي؟
w ummak? bitizʿal? bitibchi?
And your mum? Will she be upset? Will she cry?
B
شوي، أكيد. بس بتتعود
shwayy, akīd. bas bititʿawwad
A bit, for sure. But she'll get used to it.
A

tip: Use the block together: deny firmly (wallāh il-ʿaẓīm, mub ana), reproach with a question (Sēf? mub huwa illi…?), concede with ṣaḥḥ innah … bas and maʿa inni, and repair with la, agṣid. Fahad's Kuwaiti forms are for recognising: ma lī shughul, shinu hal-ḥaraka? and ēh.
